item.title: LIVE! PFL Dubai Results, Video Highlights
item.description: Before UFC 334 kicks off later tonight (Sat., Nov. 14, 2026), featuring a Heavyweight title fight between Ciryl Gane vs. Josh Hokit , Professional Fighters League (PFL) will stage its own 265-pound title fight at PFL Dubai from inside Coca-Cola Arena in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, between Vadim Nemkov vs. Sergei Bilostenniy . Nemkov is 20-2-1, but he hasn’t competed since defeating Renan Ferreira in Dec. 2025 to win the inaugural strap ( see it again here ). As for Bilostenniy, he is on a two-fight win streak and is also coming off a knockout win over Ferreira. In the co-main event of the evening, surging Welterweight contenders Patrick Habirora and Omar El Dafrawy collide, while Sergio Pettis takes Joji Goto in a sure-fire Bantamweight banger. Also in action, Adam Borics will battle it out against Khasan Magomedsharipov at Featherweight. Many readers check in before, during and after the fights to share their thoughts on all of the action, as the main card kicks off at 1 p.m. ET on the ESPN App and ESPN2 . Feel free to leave a comment (or several) about the bouts and chat with all the other Maniacs during the show — it’s always a lot of fun! item.title: An examination of whether the Commanders can stay in the NFC East race
item.description: The Commanders emerged with a victory over the Giants on Thursday night in a positively-have-to-have-it moment that saved their season. You’ve probably read that line in every recap/analysis of Washington’s 24-21 win at MetLife Stadium, including my past-midnight musings on this very site. There’s an important clause missing from that first sentence. Let’s try again: The Commanders emerged with a victory over the Giants on Thursday night in a positively-have-to-have-it moment that saved their season. … For now. The Commanders are back in the NFC East race . Can they stay there? Is their improved play sustainable? That’s the real question moving forward. Only time will tell us the answer. We can’t create a prediction model for this odd duck of a team, which features real talent, intriguing, modern schemes and a bunch of humans who can’t seem to get out of their own way. “We’ve held ourselves back,” Commanders receiver Stefon Diggs said. “When we play complementary football, we execute at a high level on offense. We move the ball just fine. We have enough playmakers. We had to execute at a high level.” Diggs was referring to that decisive Thursday night drive , where he and Daniels generated a season-altering 32-yard touchdown. He could’ve been talking about the season overall. While the injury situation has delivered body blows and haymakers, 3-5-1 is a product of Washington’s own making. Improved outcomes can also be a Commanders creation. Getting enough of them is the hard part. It’s a possibility, though maybe not a high probability considering what we’ve experienced to this point. There are some gateways to success down the stretch, but are there enough? Let’s discuss a few. The schedule is chief among them. If Washington can upset Cincinnati in Week 11, a real run is possible. The Commanders play the Cardinals, Titans, Texans and Falcons (in that order) after that. Those are all beatable teams with the right execution level. Then there’s this resurgent defense , which is figuring out how to execute Daronte Jones’ scheme. The play caller himself seems to be dialed in on what works and when to turn up the heat. The results aren’t perfect but they’re better, with point totals going down and pressure rates going northward. That scheme and the fact that Sonny Styles and Frankie have owned the midfield and Nick Cross and Trey Amos have fortified the secondary. And then there’s the Jayden Daniels of it all. The 2024 season wasn’t so long ago that we can’t recall how the quarterback played and dominated late-game situations . While he has played a role in this disappointment we call the season’s first half, he can be responsible for a resurgence that puts Washington atop this wide-open division. You’ve probably read that line in every recap/analysis of Washington’s 24-21 win at MetLife Stadium, including my past-midnight musings on this very site. The Commanders are back in the NFC East race . Can they stay there? Is their improved play sustainable? That’s the real question moving forward. Only time will tell us the answer. We can’t create a prediction model for this odd duck of a team, which features real talent, intriguing, modern schemes and a bunch of humans who can’t seem to get out of their own way. “We’ve held ourselves back,” Commanders receiver Stefon Diggs said. “When we play complementary football, we execute at a high level on offense. He could’ve been talking about the season overall. While the injury situation has delivered body blows and haymakers, 3-5-1 is a product of Washington’s own making. If Washington can upset Cincinnati in Week 11, a real run is possible. The Commanders play the Cardinals, Titans, Texans and Falcons (in that order) after that. That scheme and the fact that Sonny Styles and Frankie have owned the midfield and Nick Cross and Trey Amos have fortified the secondary. And then there’s the Jayden Daniels of it all. The 2024 season wasn’t so long ago that we can’t recall how the quarterback played and dominated late-game situations . While he has played a role in this disappointment we call the season’s first half, he can be responsible for a resurgence that puts Washington atop this wide-open division. We could come up with a gnarly cons list as well, one that’s probably a bit longer. It would include inconsistent offensive line play and the fact Washington can’t seem to get the run game going with or without Bill Croskey-Merritt. The pre-snap penalties and mental mistakes decreased against the Giants but remain a drive-killing issue that isn’t fixed. And the offensive growing plans won’t suddenly stop under rookie offensive coordinator David Blough. We’ll also meet some teams down the stretch, most notably the Vikings and Jaguars where they’ll face a real talent disparity. Let’s not create illusions that Washington is a conference contender. But they care capable of making things interesting in a relatively lightweight NFC East. Do you think the Commanders can seriously contend for a division title? Or is this a positive moment in an otherwise frustrating campaign? Let us know in the comments below.

item.title: Dawn Greenhalgh, Canadian Stage Veteran Who Voiced the Queen in ‘Babar,’ Dies at 93
item.description: Dawn Greenhalgh, a veteran Canadian actress of stage, film and television, died Nov. 6 in Toronto. She was 93. Born in Shanghai, China, she spent her childhood with her family in a Japanese prisoner of war camp, where she discovered a love for music, theater and dance. Greenhalgh moved to Canada with only a guardian […]

item.title: RAF Abu Dhabi live stream results, discussion and video highlights | Khamzat vs. Weidman
item.description: Real American Freestyle (RAF) returns TODAY (Sat.., Nov. 14 2026), with RAF Abu Dhabi , streaming live on FOX Nation from inside Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi, UAE. In the main event, former UFC Middleweight champion, Khamzat Chimaev , takes on fellow former Middleweight kingpin, Chris Weidman , who is stepping in on short notice for Colby Covington . In the co-main event, top UFC Lightweight contender, Arman Tsarukyan , takes on former Bellator veteran, Neiman Gracie . In addition, recently jumped Merab Dvalishvili collides with Marlon Moraes , Zabit Magomedsharipov makes his promotional debut against Giga Chikadze and the daughter of Frank Mir and super prospect, Bella Mir , takes on Kennedy Blaydes for the Women’s Middleweight Championship. RAF Abu Dhabi kicks off at 11 a.m. ET , streaming exclusively on FOX Nation . Whether you’re looking for live results, real-time round updates, or community discussions, below you’ll find updates, highlights, and conversation throughout the evening. RAF Abu Dhabi Results and Highlights: RAF Abu Dhabi Main Event 215 lbs.: Khamzat Chimaev vs. Chris Weidman – RAF Light Heavyweight Crossover Championship RAF Abu Dhabi Co-Main Event Catchweight: Arman Tsarukyan vs. Neiman Gracie – Crossover RAF Abu Dhabi Main Card 165 lbs.: Zabit Magomedsharipov vs. Giga Chikadze – Magomedsharipov defeats Chikadze via Pin, Round 2 View this post on Instagram 215 lbs.: Abdulrashid Sadulaev vs. Dauren Kurugliev — Sadulaev defeats Kurugliev via Points (8-5) RAF Light Heavyweight Championship View this post on Instagram 190 lbs.: Kyle Dake vs. Alp Arslan Begenjov – Dake defeats Begenjov via Tech Fall (11-0) for the RAF Cruiserweight Championship View this post on Instagram 155 lbs.: Urijah Faber vs. Saba Lazishvili – Lazishvili defeats Faber via Points (12-5) View this post on Instagram 175 lbs.: Jordan Burroughs vs. Azamat Nurykau – Burroughs defeats Nurykau via Tech Fall (11-0) View this post on Instagram 215 lbs.: Kyle Snyder vs. Shamil Erdogan – Snyder defeats Erdogan via Tech Fall (11-0) View this post on Instagram 150 lbs.: Diana Avsaragova vs. Julianna Pena – Avsaragova defeats Pena via Pin (Round 1) View this post on Instagram 215 lbs.: Murtaza Talha vs. Osama Elsaidy – Talha defeats Elsaidy via Points (10-4) Catchweight: Merab Dvalishvili vs. Marlon Moraes – Dvalishvili defeats Moraes via Pin (Round 1 ) View this post on Instagram 190 lbs.: Zahid Valencia vs. Khidir Saipudinov – Valencia defeats Saipudinov via Points 4-2 View this post on Instagram 150 lbs.: Kennedy Blades vs. Bella Mir – Blades defeats Mir via Tech Fall (10-0) for Women’s Middleweight Championship View this post on Instagram For much more on RAF and wrestling news click here .

item.title: “The Miracle Worker” May Have Set Unrealistic Expectations
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - JULY 26: Luis Morales #19 of the Athletics pitches against the Minnesota Twins during the sixth inning of the game at Target Field on July 26, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Anne Sullivan then moved Helen Keller’s hand to feel the running water from the stream. “Waa—ter!!!” Helen exclaimed intensely. “Also the ghost runner is stooopid!!!!” “That’s enough for today,” Anne replied. “And yes, you’re right, it’s really dumb.” Anne Sullivan was an incredible trailblazer for what’s possible in an impossible situation, somehow teaching someone who was blind and deaf how to recognize and pronounce words. This was a task only slightly easier than getting A’s pitchers to keep the ball in park while not walking everyone. Enter Taylor Smith, who did not write “Cruel Summer” and is trying to avoid another one, and Cam Castro, who will try to do his job with Fidel-ity. They are charged with taking the A’s to the next level, a task that will involve turning the pitching staff from one of the worst in the business to one that performs at a level better than their home ballpark. Be plenty optimistic that these two imports know a ton about pitching, about developing talent, about bringing out the best in players. But also be realistic that they are not about to replace Anne Sullivan on the “Top 10 ‘Believe it or Not’” lists. One easy proclamation to make is that “Phew, finally we can expect Luis Morales and Jack Perkins to harness their stuff and pitch like Logan Henderson and Freddy Peralta!” But fixes are not simple matters when you are dealing with what is (or isn’t) between a pitcher’s ears, mechanics their body has internalized that you are trying to “unlearn,” pitchers who may or may not be fully receptive to your preaching, and the reality that “stuff” and “how well you can pitch” just don’t always correlate. If the premise is “nowhere to go but up,” that the previous regime left every young pitcher stalled and hopeless, Luis Medina and JT Ginn offer a couple quick counterarguments. Similarly, the Brewers and Rays and Red Sox all have failed prospects in their histories whose performance just never played up to their stuff. It’s just the nature of the beast. In other words, even the Rays couldn’t fix Joe Boyle’s control so don’t put all your bullpen hopes in Luke Little’s left arm. Another hope is to go outside the organization for an infusion of pitching talent, be it proven, “MLB ready,” local or international. As inspiring as it might be to hear that the A’s “plan to be aggressive” starting at some unnamed point that could be now, obstacles abound. In luring free agents, the A’s will face one more season in a AAA park and are coming off of 98 losses no matter how they came by it. Payroll may be increasing but is not going to rival the top 10 spenders. The bigger free agent deals are known to generally be unwise investments and this off-season most everyone is seeking startin

The bigger free agent deals are known to generally be unwise investments and this off-season most everyone is seeking starting pitching creating a “player’s market”. So to land someone worth getting excited about, you probably have to accept a player-friendly deal that wipes out much of your existing payroll flexibility for a contract you will later regret. It’s basically “a more expensive Luis Severino”. In terms of trade, in order to add meaningful starting pitching the A’s would almost certainly have to part with a current key position player, e.g., Shea Langeliers, Tyler Soderstrom, Zack Gelof, or a coveted minor leaguer expected to contribute mightily to the team as soon as 2028, e.g., Leo De Vries, Jamie Arnold, Drew Burress. Perhaps the best bet is an MLB-ready SP not yet proven, the next Dan Haren — who could also be the next Dan Meyer, an equally touted pitcher only he got hurt and was never the same. The type of pitcher the A’s may well have targeted when they were at AAA would be, I don’t know, Luis Morales and Jack Perkins? Long term, Smith and Castro figure to greatly improve the A’s pitching through enhancement of the very way they draft, develop, and train pitchers from the ground up. But whether they can spin their magic to turn the current group into gems, whether they can bring in enough talent move the needle in the coming year — you might need Anne Sullivan for that and she’s been, er, retired for 90 years.

item.title: Dolphins fan confidence climbs following Lions game, ahead of Week 10 at Colts
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 08: Ollie Gordon II #0 of the Miami Dolphins in action against the Detroit Lions at Hard Rock Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins have won just one game over the first nine weeks of the 2026 NFL season. Having already passed their bye week, the Dolphins are 1-7, which would typically lead to a frustrated fanbase itching for change. This year, for the Dolphins, however, the fans seem to be accepting that this is only the first season of a long-term rebuild, understanding that losses now may lead to victories in the future. Things are not all well in Miami, though. This week, two major pieces of the starting lineup landed on injured reserve. Quarterback Malik Willis heads to the sideline for at least four weeks with a groin injury; season-ending surgery hasn’t been ruled out, but there is hope he can return in a few weeks. The news was not as good for defensive tackle Zach Sieler, who tore his biceps muscle last week. The injury occurred on the first snap of Miami’s game against the Detroit Lions, but the veteran played through it for the rest of the game. Now he will undergo surgery and will need around six months of recovery time before he is cleared to return to football activities. Miami faces the Indianapolis Colts tomorrow as the NFL’s Week 10 schedule continues. Despite Indianapolis struggling this year, earning just two wins against seven losses in the first half of the season, the oddsmakers see the Colts still likely to win this game. The latest FanDuel Sportsbook odds have the Colts favored by 3.5 points over Miami. Dolphins fan confidence The highlight of the season for the Dolphins came in Week 7, when they beat the New York Jets. Our Week 8 SB Nation Reacts fan confidence survey reflected the victory with a 97 percent positive rating for the Dolphins. It was the high-water mark of the year, and the only week in which our survey topped the 90 percent mark. At least until this week. Going toe-to-toe with the Detroit Lions for much of Week 9 encouraged the fans that brighter days are coming. The survey opened before the news of the injuries to Willis and Sieler broke, but then ran throughout the rest of the week, and it remained up above 90 percent all week. When the poll closed, 91 percent of the responses indicated the Dolphins are headed in the right direction. How will tomorrow’s game against the Colts affect next week’s survey? We will be back early next week to ask for your updated confidence in Miami’s direction. item.description: Arman Tsarukyan battles Neiman Gracie at RAF Abu Dhabi | Real American Freestyle This is the live blog for Arman Tsarukyan vs. Neiman Gracie, the catchweight co-main event for Saturday’s RAF Abu Dhabi wrestling event at Etihad Arena. Tsarukyan, the current RAF middleweight crossover champion, competes in a non-title match just a few weeks removed from his tech fall championship win over Dillon Danis at RAF 14 in Las Vegas. “Batman” is 8-1 in the promotion, including tech fall wins over Tony Ferguson, Urijah Faber, and Lance Palmer. item.title: Mavericks Streak Ends In 39-Point Blowout As Defense Collapses
item.description: Jesse Johnson-Imagn Images The Dallas Mavericks saw their three-game winning streak end in a crushing defeat on Thursday night at Target Center. Minnesota Timberwolves guard LaMelo Ball and backup Bones Hyland combined for 11 three-pointers as the Timberwolves scored 133 points to beat Dallas 94. This loss dropped the Mavericks to a 7-5 record and marked their worst performance of the season by a wide margin. Coach Dusty May admitted after the game that his team could not match the intensity of the Minnesota squad. The Timberwolves dominated the paint with 74 points and forced 19 turnovers from Dallas. This loss highlighted major issues with Dallas defense and ball handling that will require immediate attention from the coaching staff and players alike. Minnesota Defense Disrupts Every Dallas Play The primary reason for the loss was the aggressive pressure applied by the Minnesota defense. Dallas coach Dusty May stated that the Timberwolves were extremely disruptive with their point of attack defense and activity on and off the ball. He noted that Minnesota deserved to win the game based on their defensive effort alone. The Timberwolves entered the game ranked first in the league for defensive efficiency, allowing only 106.1 points per 100 possessions. Dallas struggled to get clean catches against this pressure, especially in pick-and-roll situations. According to Synergy Sports data, the Mavericks earned just 0.524 points per possession when Minnesota kept one defender on the ball handler. This pressure forced Dallas into 19 turnovers, with 10 of those coming directly from steals. The Timberwolves also blocked seven shots and held Dallas to just 37.2 percent shooting from the field. May explained that the team speed and intensity of Minnesota made it difficult for Dallas to sustain any offensive rhythm. He pointed out that having two rim protectors behind the perimeter defenders was a luxury that Dallas could not overcome. The Mavericks failed to make enough better screens or increase their pace to counteract the defensive schemes used by the Timberwolves throughout the night. Cooper Flagg And Kyrie Irving Struggle To Score Key Dallas players Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving combined for only 22 points on 9-of-23 shooting during the game. The quiet performance in Minneapolis was especially disappointing for these two players, who had combined for 78 points three nights earlier in a win over the Indiana Pacers. Irving recorded a minus-36 rating, which was the worst mark on either team and reflected the struggles of the Mavericks while he was on the court. Neither player saw action in the fourth quarter as the game was already out of reach. May observed that Minnesota possessed a single body before crossing half-court, a circumstance that stopped Dallas from utilizing that focus to create offensive opportunities in other areas. The lack of scoring from these primary options forced other players to step up, but the overall team shooting remained poor.

The quiet performance in Minneapolis was especially disappointing for these two players, who had combined for 78 points three nights earlier in a win over the Indiana Pacers. Irving recorded a minus-36 rating, which was the worst mark on either team and reflected the struggles of the Mavericks while he was on the court. Neither player saw action in the fourth quarter as the game was already out of reach. May observed that Minnesota possessed a single body before crossing half-court, a circumstance that stopped Dallas from utilizing that focus to create offensive opportunities in other areas. The lack of scoring from these primary options forced other players to step up, but the overall team shooting remained poor. Dallas finished the game shooting just 27.1 percent from three-point range, converting only 13 of 48 attempts. This inability to score efficiently against a top-tier defense left the Mavericks unable to keep pace with the high-scoring Minnesota offense. Bones Hyland And LaMelo Ball Lead Minnesota Attack Minnesota guard Bones Hyland scored 24 points off the bench while LaMelo Ball added 22 points and nine assists for the Timberwolves. The two guards combined to hit 11 of their 16 three-point attempts, providing the perimeter scoring that Dallas could not match. Hyland made several shots off the bounce from three-point range, exploiting the defensive lapses of the Mavericks. During the second quarter, Ball helped build a lead by hitting two step-back three-pointers from 25 and 27 feet within 1:16. The Timberwolves entered the third quarter with a 15-point lead and extended it significantly as Dallas could not stop the bleeding. By demonstrating excellent ball movement and unselfish play, Minnesota ended with 33 assists on 52 field goals. Coach May praised the depth of the Minnesota team, noting that their second unit injected a lot of life into the starters. The Timberwolves scored 133 points on 57.8 percent shooting from the field. Third Quarter Collapse Turns Game Into Blowout The game effectively ended when Minnesota outscored Dallas 36-17 in the third quarter. After Jaden McDaniels contributed eight points and six rebounds in the period, the Timberwolves had already opened the half with a 10-1 run to establish a 77-53 lead. This quarter turned a competitive game into a 39-point loss for the Mavericks. May said the most disappointing aspect of the game was the way Dallas responded to the runs made by Minnesota. Once the floodgates opened, the explosive speed and athleticism of the Timberwolves overwhelmed the Mavericks. The team failed to make stops when it mattered most, allowing Minnesota to extend their lead to as many as 44 points. Dallas managed to cut the deficit to one point early in the second quarter but could not sustain that energy. The Timberwolves answered a Dallas run with a timeout and then closed the half on a 24-10 run. This inability to respond to runs and maintain defensive intensity for four quarters was a major factor in the blowout. Dallas Fails To Match Physical Play Style Minnesota dominated the physical aspects of the game, scoring 74 points in the paint and winning the rebounding battle 50-38. The Mavericks allowed the Timberwolves to score 12 points off their eight turnovers in the first half alone. This physical dominance continued throughout the game as Minnesota controlled the interior and the glass. From the outset, Naji Marshall observed that the game was physical at the point of attack, finishing with 13 points and four assists. He admitted that Dallas did not do enough early in the game and that Minnesota punched them in the mouth. Marshall emphasized that the team needs to get more physical and put more pressure on the ball to stop Minnesota from getting comfortable. The Mavericks also struggled with their spacing and screening, running only six handoffs and logging just one possession off screens all night. Marshall suggested that better screens and more pace were necessary to counter the defensive pressure. The lack of physical engagement allowed Minnesota to dictate the tempo and style of the game from the opening tip. Coaching Criticism Of Team Response To Runs Coach Dusty May was critical of how his team reacted to the runs made by the Timberwolves. He stated that the response to the runs was the most disappointing thing about the game. May felt that if the Mavericks could have sustained their small-ball lineup performance, the game could have been closer at halftime. May explained that the team became impatient once Minnesota started making shots. He noted that the Mavericks gave up easy baskets by falling asleep on defense, which allowed the Timberwolves to hit step-back threes. These mistakes put Dallas in a tough spot that they could not recover from during the game. The coach also mentioned that the team was not connected on the defensive end. He said that the players needed to help each other out and communicate better on the court. This lack of connection led to open looks for Minnesota and a breakdown in the defensive scheme that Dallas had prepared for the game. Rebounding Disadvantage Hurts Dallas Effort The Mavericks were outrebounded by a significant margin of 50 to 38, which gave Minnesota extra possessions and scoring opportunities. This rebounding disparity allowed Minnesota to control the pace of the game and limit Dallas’ second-chance points. Minnesota finished with 26 fast-break points, taking advantage of the turnovers and missed shots by Dallas. Although the Mavericks tallied seven blocks and nine steals, their lack of team rebounding meant these individual defensive efforts were insufficient. The inability to secure defensi

item.title: Football pitch ruined by 'selfish' vandals in car
item.description: Bispham Junior Football Federation said their children's football pitch had been ruined by vandals [LDRS] A football pitch has been ruined by "selfish" vandals in a car, a youth team has said. Bispham Junior Football Federation in Blackpool said a vehicle was seen driving around in circles on to the pitch on Wednesday night before a person got out and tore up the grass. Chairman Lisa Hannigan said the club was due to host matches on the pitch on Saturday and Sunday, but they had to be moved due to the unplayable state of the turf. "We don't know if they intentionally set out to damage the pitch but it looks that way," Hannigan said. "It makes me angry to think someone could be so selfish and not consider the implications of their actions." 'Protective measures' Hannigan said the damage left the club "frantically" trying to rearrange plans with the other clubs and Blackpool and District Youth Football League officials to avoid cancelling the games altogether. "They potentially deprived young sports people the chance to play the game they love," she said. "It caused major disruption because the games have had to be played elsewhere. "There is no way the damaged pitch can be played on in that state." It is understood Lancashire Police are investigating the incident, the Local Democracy Reporting Service said. Looking to the future, Bispham Junior Football Federation said it was liaising with landowners Blackpool Council to see if security measures at the pitches could be bolstered. "We'd like some kind of protective measures, possibly fencing or boulders, to make it more difficult to get vehicles on the pitches," Hannigan said. Deputy leader of Blackpool Council Jane Hugo said the authority was working with police to identify those involved. item.title: Former national champion amateur boxer Joscelyn Olayo-Munoz turning pro
item.description: Las Cruces standout boxer Joscelyn Olayo-Munoz is set to make her much-anticipated professional debut. The 19-year-old Olayo-Munoz will fight Dec. 17 in Colorado Springs, Colo., on a Ghost Town Promoted card. Olayo-Munoz will fight her first pro fight in the minimumweight division of 102 pounds in a four round fight. No opponent has been announced. "I can't wait to get going in my pro career, I'm ready," Olayo-Munoz said. "It's my goal to be a world champion and I learned so much as an amateur to get to this point." Olayo-Munoz was a 17-time national champion a nd represented the United States in international competition, where she won on that level as well. Olayo-Munoz also served as a team captain for Team USA. "Joscelyn is ready and she has so much potential moving forward," said Danny Melendrez, who is Olayo-Munoz's coach and stepfather. "She has a great passion for the sport." Felix F. item.title: Mohit Ulva stars as India U19 chase down 338 in last-ball thriller to beat Pakistan by one wicket and clinch Asia Cup title
item.description: In a final that had everything, India U19 pulled off a sensational one-wicket victory over Pakistan to clinch the Under-19 Asia Cup title in a last-ball thriller on Saturday. Just when the defending champions looked certain to seal the trophy, number 10 batter Mohit Ulva produced a breathtaking unbeaten 49 off just 26 balls to guide India home in a remarkable 339-run chase. India, who were chasing a daunting target of 338, finished at 339/9 in 49.6 overs, with Ulva smashing the winning boundary off the final delivery. Chigurupati Venkata remained unbeaten on 11 as the Indian players stormed onto the field to celebrate an unforgettable triumph. Usman Khan's century powers Pakistan to 337/9 Earlier, opener Usman Khan led Pakistan's batting effort with a brilliant 107 off 106 balls, helping the defending champions post 337/9 in their allotted 50 overs. Usman shared a 62-run opening stand with Hayam Khan before combining with Abdul Qadir for a massive 135-run partnership. Qadir played an aggressive knock of 80 off just 54 deliveries, bringing up his maiden Youth ODI half-century in 39 balls. Captain Farhan Yousaf added further impetus with a 60-run contribution off 63 deliveries, taking Pakistan past the 300-run mark. For India, Kavya Patel was the standout bowler with four wickets for 68 runs, while C Venkata claimed three wickets for 40 runs. Sehwag continued his impressive tournament with a fluent 58 off 61 deliveries, including nine boundaries. Despite taking a blow on his forearm during the powerplay, the opener battled through the discomfort and brought up another half-century. Raichandani provided stability at the other end, registering his third half-century of the tournament. The Indian skipper eventually departed for a well-made 80 off 101 balls, with Anvay Dravid following him back to the pavilion after being run out for 19. VK Vineeth contributed 24 before falling to Rizwanullah, who also dismissed Arjun Rajput for 16. Pakistan continued to chip away at the Indian batting order, leaving the chase in serious trouble. Mohit Ulva produces a stunning rescue act India's hopes took another major hit when Yashbardhan Chauhan and Kavya Patel departed in quick succession. With wickets falling at regular intervals, Pakistan appeared firmly in control of the contest. However, Manal Chauhan and Mohit Ulva had other plans. He smashed Mohammad Sayyam for two boundaries and a six in the 49th over, reducing the equation to eight runs from the final six deliveries. Last-ball drama as India snatch victory With Pakistan needing just one wicket to seal the title, Ahmed Hussain was handed the responsibility of bowling the final over. Ulva and Venkata kept their composure under immense pressure, collecting crucial singles to bring the equation down to three runs off the final delivery. With the match hanging in the balance, Ulva stepped down the track and smashed Hussain's delivery towards wide long-off. The ball bounced once before racing to the boundary, sparking wild celebrations in the Indian camp. Ulva remained unbeaten on 49 off 26 balls, agonisingly missing out on a half-century but delivering one of the most memorable knocks in an India-Pakistan age-group final. India finished at 339/9 to complete a remarkable one-wicket victory and lift the Under-19 Asia Cup trophy in dramatic fashion.

item.content:encoded: Mandatory Credit: Scott Marshall-Imagn Images Cade Cunningham just had the best game of his NBA career, and now he has to face Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo . That’s a pretty good matchup for Saturday night, especially with both teams playing well lately. The Detroit Pistons will visit the Miami Heat at the Kaseya Center on November 14, at 8:00 p.m. ET. The Pistons are 8-3, third in the East with a 5-1 road record, after beating the Washington Wizards 144-140 in double overtime on Thursday . Cunningham is putting up 25.0 points, 5.2 rebounds, and 7.9 assists per game, while Duncan Robinson has 18.1 points, 1.9 rebounds, and 2.2 assists. Cunningham also scored 52 points against Washington, his career high. Miami is 6-6, seventh in the East with a 2-3 home record, after beating the Cleveland Cavaliers 133-121 on Friday . Antetokounmpo leads the team with 28.5 points, 12.3 rebounds, and 4.9 assists per game, while Adebayo is getting 19.4 points, 8.8 rebounds, and 3.2 assists. The Pistons won their first meeting 128-111 on October 23, but Miami has won three straight since starting the season 0-4. Injury Report Heat Giannis Antetokounmpo: Probable (right wrist sprain) Vladislav Goldin: Out (G League two-way) Pelle Larsson: Doubtful (illness) Klay Thompson: Probable (left ankle sprain) Pistons Jalen Duren: Out (right hamstring strain) Elijah Harkless: Available (G League two-way) Isaiah Joe: Out (right hip contusion) Isaac Jones: Available (G League two-way) Chaz Lanier: Out (G League assignment) Ebuka Okorie: Out (G League assignment) Ugonna Onyenso: Out (G League two-way) Why The Heat Have The Advantage Miami has been playing much better lately, and its offense is finally getting going. The Heat are scoring 117.2 points per game, seventh in the NBA, compared to Detroit’s 115.5, which ranks 12th. They just scored 133 against the Cavaliers, with Giannis and Bam putting up 37 points each. That’s 74 points from those two big men alone, and Detroit could have a hard time defending them without Duren. Giannis is shooting 58.3% from the field this season, while Adebayo is making 52.8%. Both players can score near the basket, and Miami should keep attacking inside if Detroit can’t stop them. The Heat also have more players helping offensively. Davion Mitchell just had 22 points and 17 assists against Cleveland, while rookie Ryan Conwell scored 20 off the bench. Miami had four players score at least 20 points in that game, and that’s a good sign before facing one of the league’s best defenses. The only problem is that Miami played last night, so the Heat are on the second night of a back-to-back. Detroit had an extra day off, although its last game went to double overtime. Still, playing at home and having Giannis available should give Miami a good chance. Why The Pistons Have The Advantage Detroit has been one of the best defensive teams in the NBA, and that’s a huge reason for its 8-3 record. The Pistons are allowing only 107.8 points per game, seventh in the league, while Miami is giving up 120.1, ranking 26th. Detroit also has a 106.7 defensive rating, fourth in the NBA, compared to Miami’s 116.2, which ranks 25th. And Cunningham has been playing some great basketball. He just scored 52 points with 11 assists and zero turnovers against the Wizards, making 16 of his 25 shots. He’s the first player to finish with at least 50 points and 10 assists without a turnover since the NBA started tracking turnovers in 1977. Miami has Davion Mitchell, but stopping Cunningham won’t be easy. The Pistons are also shooting much better from outside this season. They’re making 13.7 threes per game while shooting 37.0% from three, and Robinson has been a huge part of that. He’s making 43.7% of his threes and hitting 4.1 per game. If Miami focuses too much on Cunningham, Robinson should get plenty of open shots. Detroit already beat Miami by 17 points earlier this season, so the Pistons know they can win this matchup. Duren being out is a problem, especially against Giannis and Adebayo, but Detroit still has Paul Reed, Ausar Thompson , and John Collins to help inside. X-Factors Thompson has been doing a little bit of everything for Detroit. He’s getting 10.1 points, 8.7 rebounds, and 5.1 assists per game while shooting 49.4% from the field. Thompson just had 17 points, 11 rebounds, and 11 assists against Washington, and the Pistons need that kind of game again. He’ll probably spend plenty of time defending Giannis, so his defense and rebounding will be very important. Daniss Jenkins has also been playing well, putting up 13.5 points, 3.8 rebounds, and 4.3 assists per game while shooting 44.4% from three. He scored 21 points against the Wizards, and Detroit needs his scoring with Isaiah Joe out. If Jenkins makes a few threes and helps Cunningham handle the ball, the Pistons should have a better chance against Miami’s defense. For the Heat, Mitchell could be one of the most important players tonight. He’s getting 16.9 points, 2.3 rebounds, and 9.2 assists per game while shooting 49.7% from the field. Mitchell just had 17 assists against Cleveland, and he’ll need to keep finding Giannis and Adebayo near the basket. His defense against Cunningham will also be a huge part of this game. Ryan Conwell could have another good night off the bench, especially with Larsson doubtful. The rookie just scored 20 points against the Cavaliers, and Miami needs more shooting around Giannis. Detroit has been great defensively, so Conwell needs to make his open shots whenever Cunningham and the other Pistons defenders help inside. Prediction I’m taking the Pistons in a close game. Miami has been playing much better, and Giannis could have a huge night with Duren out, but Detroit has been the better defensive team. The Pistons rank fourth in defensive rating, while the Heat are 25th, and Cunningham is coming off a 52-point game. Miami might keep this close with Giannis and Adebayo scoring inside, but I think Cunningham and Robinson will do enough to get another win. Prediction: Heat vs. Pistons 113-117

item.title: Man United Women make it 12 unbeaten with comfortable 2-0 win over Crystal Palace
item.description: Man United Women make it 12 unbeaten with comfortable 2-0 win over Crystal Palace Manchester United Women welcomed Crystal Palace to the Progress with Unity Stadium. First half Elisabeth Terland had the hosts’ first chance, but her effort from distance sailed over the bar. Phallon Tullis-Joyce had to pull off an impressive stop to keep her side level at the near post. Terland broke through and put the ball past the keeper, but it was ruled out for offside. The Norwegian was close again, but her effort trickled just wide of the post. Finally, Manchester United captain Maya Le Tissier broke the deadlock. Manchester United midfielder Jess Park picked out Le Tissier, who smashed a strike into the bottom corner from 25 yards to perfectly mark her 150th match as a Red Devil. Jess Park, Julia Zigiotti and Simi Awujo all went close to scoring, but the Palace defence held firm and made an impressive stop on each occasion. Second half Palace started the second half with vigour, and Bethany England went close with a shot, but it trickled just wide of the goal. Le Tissier flicked the ball towards goal, but her effort went just wide. In the 65th minute, United made the game much more comfortable when they scored their second. Park played in Elisabeth Terland , and she kept her cool to slot the ball past the Palace keeper. The game became more transitional, and Lea Schüller almost added a third, but her shot went just over the crossbar. The match petered out in a 2-0 win, and Eva Olid’s side made it 12 matches unbeaten in all competitions. United now find themselves fourth and just one point behind the Champions League places and London City Lionesses. Man United Women results 26/27 Featured image by Ben Roberts Photo via Getty Images

item.title: ‘Everything a coach wants:’ UGA football commit dies after medical emergency
item.description: ‘Everything a coach wants:’ UGA football commit dies after medical emergency Rabun Gap-Nacoochee School A Georgia high school community is mourning the loss of a standout student-athlete who was preparing to take the next step toward his dream of playing college football. [DOWNLOAD: Free WSB-TV News app for alerts as news breaks ] Marcellus Young Casario, known to friends and teammates as “Mar,” died after a sudden medical emergency, Rabun Gap-Nacoochee School announced Saturday. Casario was a boarding student who came to the Rabun Gap school from Halifax, Nova Scotia, Canada, as a junior. He quickly became a beloved member of the campus community, where he was known as a natural leader, loyal friend and dedicated student-athlete. A standout defensive lineman, Casario had committed to play football at the University of Georgia, school officials said. He was looking forward to graduating from Rabun Gap in December and enrolling at UGA in January, according to school officials. His love for football started at an early age, inspired by his father and grandfather, who helped foster his passion for the game. TRENDING STORIES: Deadly deer disease detected in another Georgia county Racial slur allegations spark investigation after metro Atlanta high school flag football game Man fires several shots at Chamblee police inside motel “He was everything a coach wants in a player. Mar truly embodied our mission to ‘love one another,’” Head Football Coach Derek White said. “He was known for his relentless dedication, and his journey as a student-athlete was marked by hard work and a true brotherhood with his teammates.” Beyond football, the school said Casario was guided by his Christian faith and was an active member of its Christian Student Initiative. He often encouraged others and shared his faith with those around him. “Mar brought light, faith, and character to everything he did, and his absence is a tremendous void in our close-knit community,” Head of School Bob Ahrens said. Ahrens said the school’s thoughts and prayers are with Casario’s family in Halifax, as well as his teammates and friends. Rabun Gap said it is providing counseling, spiritual support and other care services for students, faculty and staff as they grieve. The school asked the public to respect the privacy of Casario’s family. [SIGN UP: WSB-TV Daily Headlines Newsletter ]

item.title: Thunder’s Shai Gilgeous-Alexander hilariously corrects LA reporter over AI-generated stat
item.description: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Thunder’s Shai Gilgeous-Alexander hilariously corrects LA reporter over AI-generated stat appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . AI is really getting out of hand, as most of us hardly cross-check information from a quick search. And that is what happened with an LA reporter during Shai Gilgeous-Alexander ’s press conference. The reporter relied on AI search results for a statistic about Gilgeous-Alexander’s first-half assists, only for the two-time MVP to point out the mistake. During a press conference , the reporter asked Gilgeous-Alexander about recording assists in the first half of his previous game. The guard quickly corrected him, explaining that he had finished the first half against the Portland Trail Blazers without an assist. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Shai Gilgeous-Alexander fact-checking an LA reporter who used AI search results to get an incorrect stat lmao pic.twitter.com/B4wZbSFv7B — Clemente Almanza (@CAlmanza1007) November 14, 2026 The exchange drew attention on social media, with fans praising Gilgeous-Alexander for catching the inaccurate information. However, the reporter acknowledged that the figure came from an AI search, while also laughing off the risks of relying on generated answers without checking the underlying statistics. The moment came during a difficult stretch for Oklahoma City. The Thunder recently suffered a 113-112 loss to the LA Clippers, extending their losing streak to three games for the first time in more than three years. Gilgeous-Alexander still delivered an outstanding performance , scoring 40 points on 15-of-26 shooting while adding five assists and four rebounds. He also had two opportunities to win the game in the final seconds, but neither attempt found the basket. The two-time MVP has been carrying a heavy offensive burden amid Oklahoma City’s injury problems. His performance against the Clippers showed that he can still produce at an elite level, even when the supporting cast is depleted. Related: Thunder’s Jared McCain shows limitless range with 30-foot buzzer-beater Related: Thunder’s Isaiah Hartenstein, Nikola Topic connect for textbook alley-oop dunk vs. Clippers

item.title: Why is Juan Carlos Ferrero getting more attention than ATP Finals’ players?
item.description: Juan Carlos Ferrero, also known as JCF, is the toast of the town at the 2026 ATP Finals in Turin. Carlos Alcaraz’s former coach who was set to join Ben Shelton’s team in 2027 has begun work early in Turin. JCF seems to relish the attention. It makes no sense that a coach gets more attention than the eight players, but there is where we are. MORE: What does Ben Shelton gain by hiring Carlos Alcaraz’s former coach? In addition to being in front of the cameras in Turin, he has been talking to any media person who will listen since becoming a member of Shelton’s team. Juan Carlos Ferrero in the Big T podcast has confirmed his first event where he will be coaching Ben Shelton is the world tour finals in Turin in 2 weeks time! Ferrero believes he can help Shelton take on the likes of Sinner and Alcaraz. How’ll this make you feel? item.title: FIU at Delaware in Conference USA football | Live report, updates
item.description: The Blue Hens will hope their preparation pays off at Delaware Stadium on Nov. 14, knowing that will be among a multitude of requirements needed to prevail. Their 2026 football season may be riding on it. Delaware (4-5 overall, 2-3) and Florida International (4-5, 2-3) kick off at 3 p.m. in the Conference USA game. A large Homecoming Day crowd is expected for the Blue Hens’ first Saturday home game since Sept. 19. It is being streamed on ESPN+. With a road game at New Mexico State next weekend and a season finale against Conference USA co-leader Jacksonville State looming, Delaware’s six-win bowl eligibility is in jeopardy. “Every team is good in this conference,” said Blue Hens running back Viron Ellison Jr. “We really have to prep well and it really starts Sundays after we play our game on Saturday, with recovery and mindset in preparing for the next game.” Delaware will see today if it has done what it needs to thwart the Panthers, who’ll be playing with the same desperation and determination. A frustrating 42-40 loss last week at Kennesaw State likely provided Ellison and his teammates with plenty of motivation. The Blue Hens will be looking to limit the explosive plays that have hurt them defensively while getting their offense moving against one of CUSA’s stingier units. The games matches a Delaware offense that is second in CUSA in yards per game against an FIU unit that’s second in total defense. “They're really good,” Delaware coach Ryan Carty said of the Panthers. “They pass rush really well. That’s what starts it all. Their front is extremely good. They're statistically great, but they're talented. They're not just good against the pass. They play physical in the run game. They're stout. They can hold up.” FIU’s secondary is also quite adept, Carty added, meaning quarterback Nick Minicucci will have to be on target and Delaware receivers must win their one-one-one confrontations.” “They can go make a play in some wide spaces,” Carty said, “and so we got our work cut out for us for sure.” Contact Kevin Tresolini at ktresolini@delawareonline.com and follow on Twitter @kevintresolini. item.title: How Austin Championship trophy was forged with bats, Moonlight Towers and Texas steel
item.description: AUSTIN, Texas — At their East Austin shop, Zach Henke and Justus Cogdell are used to working with steel. Big steel. Their day-to-day work includes everything from structural I-beams and cranes to custom staircases, railings and decorative vent hoods. But recently, an unexpected email brought a project unlike anything they had done before: building the trophy for the Austin Championship presented by Compliance Solutions . And the pair had to do it quickly. Tournament organizers needed a late replacement after plans for another trophy fell through, so they reached out to Henke and his team to see what they could come up with on a tight deadline. "You just don't get opportunities every day to build something like this," Henke said. Fortunately, Henke had the right guy in the shop. More: Austin Championship merchandise gets Texas makeover after Good Good sponsorship fallout Cogdell, Henke's shop manager, is also a trained blacksmith. While plenty of people spend their free time playing golf, Cogdell spends his at the forge. He got into blacksmithing at Austin Community College, where he completed a two-year specialization in sculptural blacksmithing. Since then, the craft has been his job, his hobby and, at times, a side hustle. Now he was being asked to make his first championship trophy. Organizers didn't give them many restrictions. They provided the tournament logo and asked that a bat somehow be incorporated into the trophy. Beyond that, Henke and Cogdell had room to get creative. For Cogdell, who grew up in Austin, that meant making sure there was no mistaking where the trophy came from. He sketched out a design incorporating the city's historic Moonlight Towers, then turned the requested bat into a Mexican free-tailed bat, the species famous for the massive colony that lives beneath the Congress Avenue Bridge. More: 2026 Austin Championship leaderboard, live scores, tee times, projected standings The result is a trophy loaded with Austin touches. Getting it finished, however, has turned into a race against the clock. "It's extremely fun. I love creative projects and sculpture," Cogdell said. "It was a little stressful because the timeline's really tight, but being able to go through the creative process and think about what we want to incorporate and how to make it unique to Austin, which I grew up in, was really, really fun." Cogdell has made plenty of sculptural pieces over the years, but never anything quite like this. With the Austin Championship underway, he and Henke are relishing the attention that came from a trophy that started with little more than an email, a tournament logo and a request for a bat. Soon enough, somebody at Omni Barton Creek Resort will hoist it. Tim Schmitt is the managing editor of Golfweek and the golf coordinator of the USA Today Network. This article originally appeared on Golfweek: How Austin Championship trophy was forged with bats, Moonlight Towers and Texas steel

item.title: Matt Jung injury update, Wisconsin safety carted off field vs Maryland
item.description: The Wisconsin football team has lost another one of its key defensive players to an injury. Starting safety Matt Jung exited Wisconsin's Week 11 game against Maryland on Saturday, Nov. 14, with an apparent leg injury at the end of the second quarter. The UW training staff used an air cast and carted him off the field after spending significant time on the field tending to the injury. Matt Jung injury Jung suffered the injury while making a play that realistically saved at least three points for the Badgers . Maryland had first-and-goal on Wisconsin 's 1-yard line, but then Maryland quarterback Cardell Williams fumbled the ball and Jung recovered it. Who is Matt Jung? Jung, a fifth-year safety from Neenah, has played a crucial role on the Badgers' 2026 defense. He started in every game and ranked third on the team with 64 tackles before the Maryland game, trailing only linebackers Cooper Catalano and Mason Posa. Wisconsin football injury update It was part of a rough first half for the Badgers from an injury standpoint. Posa visited the medical tent before coming back into the game. Arizona State transfer cornerback Javan Robinson also went down with an injury and was helped off the field. Those injuries are in addition to Sebastian Cheeks' injury in practice this week , which kept him out of the Maryland game. Check back later for more updates. This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: Matt Jung injury update, Wisconsin safety carted off field vs Maryland

item.title: 'The Body' Ending Explained: Is Grace Possessed? Netflix Showrunners Talk Season 2
item.description: The Body , Netflix’s new campy-horror TV series , came out this week. But based on a quick social media browse, it might as well have come out months ago. The high school thriller inspired passionate fan debates among viewers and dozens of fan cams dedicated to favorite characters long before a single episode aired. Now that The Body has finally arrived, however, fans are having an entirely different debate that hinges on its wild cliffhanger ending.

item.title: Darian Mensah’s Contract, Lawsuit Explain Leaving Duke for Miami
item.description: SOUTH BEND, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 07: Darian Mensah #10 of the Miami Hurricanes looks on against the Notre Dame Fighting Irish during the second half at Notre Dame Stadium on November 07, 2026 in South Bend, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Getty CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - DECEMBER 06: Darian Mensah #10 of the Duke Blue Devils reacts after a touchdown during overtime in the 2025 ACC Football Championship against the Virginia Cavaliers at Bank of America Stadium on December 06, 2025 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) SOUTH BEND, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 07: Darian Mensah #10 of the Miami Hurricanes celebrates a touchdown against the Notre Dame Fighting Irish during the second half at Notre Dame Stadium on November 07, 2026 in South Bend, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Darian Mensah is one of the top quarterbacks in the country, but he’s already at his third school in three seasons. Mensah began his college football career as the QB for the Tulane Green Wave. His play there earned him a big contract with the Duke Blue Devils. But after a year in Durham, a late transfer portal entry and a lawsuit, Mensah landed with the Miami Hurricanes for the 2026 season. Miami is a top-10 team, coming off its first loss of the season (at Notre Dame), and will take on Duke on Saturday. Mensah will be in the spotlight even more than usual. The 8-1 Hurricanes host the 7-2 Blue Devils in a game with intriguing ACC implications. Miami still doesn’t have Malachi Toney, making things a bit tougher on them. And there on the field trying to lead Miami to a bounceback win over Duke will be Mensah — a year removed from being a Blue Devils star. Why Darian Mensah Left Duke for Miami Getty CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA – DECEMBER 06: Darian Mensah #10 of the Duke Blue Devils reacts after a touchdown during overtime in the 2025 ACC Football Championship against the Virginia Cavaliers at Bank of America Stadium on December 06, 2025 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) Any transfer has complexity, and Mensah’s was no different. Money certainly had to play a factor, but the program history likely played a part, too. Miami has had huge success recently with transfer quarterbacks. Cam Ward came from Washington State and was the first overall pick into the NFL. Carson Beck came from Georgia and was a third-rounder. Mensah had proven in climbing the ladder from Tulane to Duke already, and then in being the most sought-after transfer QB, that he was better than anyone had expected when he was a high school recruit. He clearly wanted the highest-possible platform to prove that. Making things a bit more painful is the fact that Mensah had already affirmed he was returning to Duke before transferring. The contract offer likely was part of that. Darian Mensah’s NIL Contract at Miami Getty SOUTH BEND, INDIANA – NOVEMBER 07: Darian Mensah #10 of the Miami Hurricanes celebrates a touchdown against the Notre Dam

Darian Mensah’s NIL Contract at Miami Getty SOUTH BEND, INDIANA – NOVEMBER 07: Darian Mensah #10 of the Miami Hurricanes celebrates a touchdown against the Notre Dame Fighting Irish during the second half at Notre Dame Stadium on November 07, 2026 in South Bend, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Mensah is reported to have an agreement at $6.5 million for the 2026 season at Miami through NIL deals and overall financial arrangements. He was making $4 million per year over a two-year deal at Duke, and the Blue Devils sued him for a breach of contract for leaving after a year. A settlement was reached in late January out of court. “I remember Darian called me and was like, ‘I just got this crazy offer,'” Duke running back Nate Sheppard said recently told CBS Sports . “And I was like, well, you know, you got to do what’s best for you. If you think that’s best, then go ahead. But obviously, it was a little frustrating. We were supposed to come back, kind of repeat things.” Mensah’s answer at ACC Media Days in July? “Business is business.” And on Saturday, business will be settled on the field. item.title: Paddy Pimblett vs. Ilia Topuria? Dana White Likes the Idea of It
item.description: Paddy Pimblett Ilia Topuria Dana White Getty UFC president Dana White said that he likes the idea of a lightweight bout between two of his biggest stars, Ilia Topuria and Paddy Pimblett. Topuria is set to return to the UFC Octagon in early 2027, and he has been connected to a matchup against Pimblett, his long-time rival. It seems like White, the one who makes the ultimate decision about what big fights the UFC books, likes the sound of this matchup. Dana White Likes a Paddy Pimblett vs. Ilia Topuria Fight Speaking to Bleacher Report, White said he would be down for Pimblett vs. Topuria. “Paddy Pimblett versus Ilia Topuria is a huge fight that makes sense and can happen and should happen. Those are the kind of fights I like talking about,” White said. 🚨Dana White says Ilia Topuria vs. Paddy Pimblett is a “HUGE FIGHT” that can and should happen. “Paddy Pimblett versus Ilia Topuria is a huge fight that makes sense and can happen and should happen. Those are the kind of fights I like talking about.” pic.twitter.com/59j6hZwMlx — Red Corner MMA (@RedCorner_MMA) November 14, 2026 Fight Makes Sense A lightweight bout between Pimblett and Topuria makes too much sense, so hopefully, the UFC gets this fight booked as soon as possible. These are two of the top lightweights in the sport right now; neither of them has a fight booked, and both of them hate each other. So, it just makes a ton of sense for this fight to get booked as soon as possible. The UFC has begun booking its fights for early 2027, and a matchup between Pimblett and Topuria would be the perfect main event for a numbered UFC event. Even if there is no belt on the line between these two, they are still two of the biggest names in the sport, and the promotion could easily justify a numbered card for the pair. So, we’ll see what happens here, but given that White seems more than thrilled with the idea of these two stepping into the Octagon against each other and scrapping, it does feel like there is very real momentum building towards the UFC booking these two against each other. If they do end up fighting, look for the fight to potentially take place in March or April as the main event of the UFC’s numbered events in either of those months, with Las Vegas, Nevada, and Phoenix, Arizona, mentioned as possible locations. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Paddy Pimblett vs. Ilia Topuria? Dana White Likes the Idea of It appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Arizona men’s cross country advances to NCAA Championships
item.description: For the first time in two decades, the Arizona men’s cross country team will be competing at the NCAA Championships. The Wildcats men advanced to next week’s national championship meet by finishing in fifth place at the NCAA West Regional on Friday. The showing was enough for Arizona to earn an at-large berth. Arizona last competed at NCAA Championships in 2006. The team took 21st place that year. Evans Tanui led Arizona on Friday with a 6th place individual finish, running a 10K time of 29:13.4. Josphat Meli took 19th with a time of 29:37.4, and Vincent Gwachi took 27th with a time of 29:50.6. Lawi Ngetich and Hanibal Haile rounded out Arizona’s five scorers. All-Region Honors for Evans Tanui! ⏱️6th Place – 29:13.4 #BearDown pic.twitter.com/7Qly8cLMDd — Arizona Track & Field/Cross Country (@ArizonaTrack) November 13, 2026 Arizona finished in a tie with Portland with 141 points, but Portland won the tiebreaker by way of total time it took its athletes to cross the finish line. Oregon won the race, followed by Washington and Stanford. On the women’s side, freshman Mercy Chepkemoi put together another standout performance, finishing runner-up in the 6K with a time of 18:59.o. By placing in the top four, Chepkemoi qualified for the NCAA Championships. All-Region Honors for Mercy Chepkemoi! ⏱️2nd Place – 18:59.0 #BearDown pic.twitter.com/ZTV6jnKeLn — Arizona Track & Field/Cross Country (@ArizonaTrack) November 13, 2026 Praise Chepkemoi finished in 10th place with a time of 19:48.5, earning her All-Region Honors. The Arizona women as a team finished in 11th place, their best showing at the West Regional since 2013. The NCAA Championships will be held Nov. 21 in Terre Haute, Ind.

item.title: International round-up: Haaland on target in important Norway win over Wales
item.description: International round-up: Haaland on target in important Norway win over Wales Erling Haaland scored the decisive third goal as Norway defeated Wales 3-1 in UEFA National League qualifying. RB Leipzig’s Antonio Nusa opened the scoring just before the hour mark with Andreas Schjelderup doubling the advantage for the hosts shortly after at Ullevaal Stadion, Haaland setting up the Benfica winger for the second goal. David Brooks pulled one back for Craig Bellamy’s men but Haaland put the contest beyond The Dragons by despatching a penalty late on after playing in Schjelderup who was fouled by Connor Roberts. The City hitman made no mistake from the spot to bring up his 66th goal for Norway. The result moved Stale Solbakken’s men up to second in League A - Group 4, six points behind leaders Portugal who host third place Denmark later this evening. The top two teams will advance to two‑legged quarter‑finals in March 2027 with the winners of those qualifying for the June 2027 Finals inclusive of semi‑finals, third‑place match and final. Portugal, two-time winners, are defending champions having beaten Spain on penalties in the 2024/25 finals, held in Germany. In the early hours of the morning UK time, Enzo Fernández played 90 minutes for Argentina as they lost 2-1 at home to Uruguay in a friendly at Estadio Alberto José Armando. Leonardo Balerdi’s own-goal allied to Maximiliano Araújo’s effort put the visitors two-up only for former Blue, Julián Alvarez to reduce arrears but it was too little, too late as La Albiceleste fell to defeat. Vitor Reis was an unused substitute as Brazil went down 3-2 to Japan at the Singapore National Stadium. Goals from Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura put the hosts in control but the visitors came back strong courtesy of a Vinícius Júnior brace. But there was late drama with Tatsuhiro Sakamoto bundling home at the death, sparking red cards for manager Carlo Ancelotti and captain Raphinha, the dismissals coming as a result of questioning why a foul hadn’t been given in favour of Joao Gomes in the build-up to that late winner. item.content:encoded: International round-up: Haaland on target in important Norway win over Wales Erling Haaland scored the decisive third goal as Norway defeated Wales 3-1 in UEFA National League qualifying. RB Leipzig’s Antonio Nusa opened the scoring just before the hour mark with Andreas Schjelderup doubling the advantage for the hosts shortly after at Ullevaal Stadion, Haaland setting up the Benfica winger for the second goal. David Brooks pulled one back for Craig Bellamy’s men but Haaland put the contest beyond The Dragons by despatching a penalty late on after playing in Schjelderup who was fouled by Connor Roberts. The City hitman made no mistake from the spot to bring up his 66th goal for Norway. The result moved Stale Solbakken’s men up to second in League A - Group 4, six points behind leaders Portugal who host third place Denmark later this evening. The top two teams will advance to two‑legged quarter‑finals in March 2027 with the winners of those qualifying for the June 2027 Finals inclusive of semi‑finals, third‑place match and final. Portugal, two-time winners, are defending champions having beaten Spain on penalties in the 2024/25 finals, held in Germany. In the early hours of the morning UK time, Enzo Fernández played 90 minutes for Argentina as they lost 2-1 at home to Uruguay in a friendly at Estadio Alberto José Armando. Leonardo Balerdi’s own-goal allied to Maximiliano Araújo’s effort put the visitors two-up only for former Blue, Julián Alvarez to reduce arrears but it was too little, too late as La Albiceleste fell to defeat. Vitor Reis was an unused substitute as Brazil went down 3-2 to Japan at the Singapore National Stadium. Goals from Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura put the hosts in control but the visitors came back strong courtesy of a Vinícius Júnior brace. item.title: Participation in Connecticut boys' high school sports fell more than 4%. Most sports saw declines.
item.description: Indoor track saw a six percent decrease in participation, fall from 5,703 boys in 2024-2025 to 5,387 in 2025-2026. (Arnold Gold/Hearst Connecticut Media) Boys high school sports in Connecticut experienced an overall decline in participation in 2025-2026, and the drop was felt across nearly all of them. Football took a big hit with a 9% drop in participation from 2024-2025 to 2025-2026. There were 8,831 boys playing football in 2024-2025, but 8,015 in 2025-2026. Overall, Connecticut saw over 4% fewer participants in 2025-2026 than it did in 2024-2025, according to CIAC numbers. There were 58,605 boys who played sports in 2024-2025, but that decreased to 55,990 in 2025-2026. Six-percent decreases were seen in swimming and indoor track. Swimming declined from 1,606 boys in 2024-2025 to 1,513 in 2025-2026. Indoor track fell from 5,703 boys in 2024-2025 to 5,387 in 2025-2026. A five-percent decrease was seen in wrestling and volleyball. Wrestling went from 2,885 boys in 2024-2025 to 2,744 in 2025-2026. Volleyball dropped from 1,474 boys in 2024-2025 to 1,397 in 2025-2026. Four-percent decreases were seen in basketball, ice hockey, lacrosse, soccer and tennis. Basketball fell from 5,272 boys in 2024-2025 to 5,042 in 2025-2026. Ice hockey dropped from 1,333 boys in 2024-2025 to 1,280 in 2025-2026. Lacrosse declined from 3,626 boys in 2024-2025 to 3,490 in 2025-2026. Soccer went down from 7,165 boys in 2024-2025 to 6,861 in 2025-2026. Tennis dipped from 2,127 boys in 2024-2025 to 2,033 in 2025-2026. There was a three-percent drop in spring golf from 1,056 boys in 2024-2025 to 1,022 in 2025-2026. Baseball fell two percent from 4,824 boys in 2024-2025 to 4,721 in 2025-2026. Cross country dipped one percent from 3,027 boys in 2024-2025 to 2,999 in 2025-2026. "I think there's a few challenges that exist in terms of maintaining participation rates here in Connecticut," CIAC executive director Glenn Lungarini said earlier this year. "We are still experiencing a decline in student population each year." Indeed, the state hit a 20-year low for public school enrollment in 2025-2026, according to data published by the Department of Education in February of this year. Outdoor track stayed nearly even with a decrease of just 12 boys from 7,535 in 2024-2025 to 7,523 in 2025-2026. One sport that increased in terms of boys participation was fall golf. There were 719 boys who played in 2025-2026, and that was a 5% increase over the 685 that took part in 2024-2025. The numbers were more positive for participation when comparing the 2023-2024 and 2024-2025 school years. Seven sports saw an increase in participation. Volleyball saw an increase of 27%, from 1,161 boys in 2023-2024 to 1,474 in 2024-2025. Swimming saw an increase of 12%, from 1,435 boys in 2023-2024 to 1,606 in 2024-2025. Indoor track participation was up 8%, from 5,268 boys in 2023-2024 to 5,703 in 2024-2025. Soccer was up by 5%, from 6,855 boys in 2023-2024 to 7,165 in 2024-2025. Basketball and tennis both

Swimming declined from 1,606 boys in 2024-2025 to 1,513 in 2025-2026. Indoor track fell from 5,703 boys in 2024-2025 to 5,387 in 2025-2026. A five-percent decrease was seen in wrestling and volleyball. Wrestling went from 2,885 boys in 2024-2025 to 2,744 in 2025-2026. Volleyball dropped from 1,474 boys in 2024-2025 to 1,397 in 2025-2026. Four-percent decreases were seen in basketball, ice hockey, lacrosse, soccer and tennis. Basketball fell from 5,272 boys in 2024-2025 to 5,042 in 2025-2026. Ice hockey dropped from 1,333 boys in 2024-2025 to 1,280 in 2025-2026. Lacrosse declined from 3,626 boys in 2024-2025 to 3,490 in 2025-2026. Soccer went down from 7,165 boys in 2024-2025 to 6,861 in 2025-2026. Tennis dipped from 2,127 boys in 2024-2025 to 2,033 in 2025-2026. There was a three-percent drop in spring golf from 1,056 boys in 2024-2025 to 1,022 in 2025-2026. Baseball fell two percent from 4,824 boys in 2024-2025 to 4,721 in 2025-2026. Cross country dipped one percent from 3,027 boys in 2024-2025 to 2,999 in 2025-2026. "I think there's a few challenges that exist in terms of maintaining participation rates here in Connecticut," CIAC executive director Glenn Lungarini said earlier this year. "We are still experiencing a decline in student population each year." Indeed, the state hit a 20-year low for public school enrollment in 2025-2026, according to data published by the Department of Education in February of this year. Outdoor track stayed nearly even with a decrease of just 12 boys from 7,535 in 2024-2025 to 7,523 in 2025-2026. One sport that increased in terms of boys participation was fall golf. There were 719 boys who played in 2025-2026, and that was a 5% increase over the 685 that took part in 2024-2025. The numbers were more positive for participation when comparing the 2023-2024 and 2024-2025 school years. Seven sports saw an increase in participation. Volleyball saw an increase of 27%, from 1,161 boys in 2023-2024 to 1,474 in 2024-2025. Swimming saw an increase of 12%, from 1,435 boys in 2023-2024 to 1,606 in 2024-2025. Indoor track participation was up 8%, from 5,268 boys in 2023-2024 to 5,703 in 2024-2025. Soccer was up by 5%, from 6,855 boys in 2023-2024 to 7,165 in 2024-2025. Basketball and tennis both saw modest increases of 2%. Wrestling was one sport that varied wildly. The sport saw 21% increases in the periods of 2021-2022 to 2022-2023 and 2022-2023 to 2023-2024. From 2023-2024 to 2024-2025, however, wrestling participation fell 8%. It fell another 5% between the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 time periods. The back-to-back 21% increases raised the numbers from 2,151 boys in 2021-2022 to 3,142 in 2023-2024. Wrestling reached its five-year participation high of 3,142 boys in 2023-2024, but it had fallen to 2,744 in 2025-2026. Volleyball is another sport that has had both big increases and decreases. Participation was up 14% from 1,058 boys in 2021-2022 to 1,209 in 2022-2023. There was a decrease of 4% to 1,161 boys in 2023-2024. That was followed by a 27% increase to a five-year high of 1,474 boys in 2024-2025. Volleyball's participation was down 5% to 1,397 boys in 2025-2026. Swimming saw one big increase of 12% from 1,435 boys in 2023-2024 to 1,606 in 2024-2025. There were back-to-back, 4% decreases (2021-2022 to 2022-2023 and 2022-2023 to 2023-2024). Swimming declined from 1,606 boys in 2024-2025 to 1,513 in 2025-2026. Indoor track saw three straight periods of strong increases (5% from 2021-2022 to 2022-2023; 8% from 2022-2023 to 2023-2024; 8% from 2023-2024 to 2024-2025). Indoor track saw its participation go from 4,649 boys in 2021-2022 all the way to a five-year high of 5,703 in 2024-2025. Those numbers were followed by a 6% decrease to 5,387 boys in 2025-2026. Baseball and lacrosse both saw decreases in each of the four time periods. Baseball stood at 5,298 boys in 2021-2022 but had fallen to 4,721 by 2025-2026 with decreases of 4% from 2021-2022 to 2022-2023, 2% from 2022-2023 to 2023-2024, 4% (2023-2024 to 2024-2025) and 2% (2024-2025 to 2025-2026). Lacrosse was at 3,880 boys in 2021-2022 but had fallen to 3,490 by 2025-2026 with decreases of 1% (2021-2022 to 2022-2023), 4% (2022-2023 to 2023-2024), 1% (2023-2024 to 2024-2025) and 4% (2024-2025 to 2025-2026). One thing Lungarini noted when the NFHS participation survey numbers came out in September was pay-to-play. Southington and Windsor both adopted such policies after June. "You're seeing more and more school districts that are in financial positions where they have to go to pay to participate," Lungarini said. "One of the negatives is when those are instituted, it does have an impact of declining participation." Sign up for the Connecticut Briefing from CT Insider. Get the biggest headlines of the day from our network of journalists around the state. This article originally published at Participation in Connecticut boys' high school sports fell more than 4%. Most sports saw declines. .

item.description: No. 8 Tennessee is ranked among the country’s top 10 for the first time this season as it travels to Texas A&M on Saturday. Nov 7, 2026; Columbia, South Carolina, USA; Texas A&M Aggies defensive end T.J. Searcy (18) celebrates a missed field goal by the South Carolina Gamecocks in the second half at Williams-Brice Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Blake-Imagn Images How to watch Tennessee vs Texas A&M Date: Saturday, November 14, 2026 Time: 3 PM EDT Channel: ESPN Stream: Fubo ( try for free ) Texas A&M is searching for its first win in nearly a month when it hosts No. 8 Tennessee at Kyle Field on Saturday. The Aggies have lost four straight on the road – all against ranked opposition – but are unbeaten in two playing at home and hope to keep that theme going when they welcome the Vols to College Station in Week 11. Tennessee makes the trip to Texas ranked inside the nation’s top 10 for the first time this term, which is well-deserved when assessing the school’s 7-2 record (4-2 in the SEC). However, it’s the manner of those two defeats that further underlines the point, losing to Texas in September (when it was ranked No. 1) by just three points before falling 27-24 to a South Carolina team that’s worked its way into CFP contention. Mike Elko’s Texas A&M team also dropped to South Carolina last weekend, though quarterback Marcel Reed was unable to convert a touchdown despite the team generating more than 450 scrimmage yards. The 4-5 Aggies are stuck with just the one SEC victory to their name this campaign, leaving Tennessee with a gaping opportunity to secure its first-ever win at College Station in only its second trip, the first having ended in a double overtime win for the hosts in 2016. The Vols boast the 10th-best scoring defense in the country (18th overall) and allow the opposition just 15.1 points per game on average this season. Texas A&M has averaged 15 points scored across its past five games against FBS opposition but will need home advantage to work overtime on Saturday if it’s to halt Tennessee’s rise up the rankings. item.title: Cam Newton says he’s now changed his mind on the rule change coming into college football
item.description: Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images Cam Newton revealed that he has finally come around to accept the new 24-team playoff format in College Football Playoffs. It was confirmed that the CFP would have 24 teams, which is an increase of 12 from the previous format. There have been many critics of the new format, as they believed it would take away the heart and soul of college football, which is the conference championship game. However, Newton, who has had some of the most legendary College Football seasons, was willing to let go of that due to what it was bringing in. “Initially, I felt like this gentleman as well. I was so devastated man, I seen and looked at my threads. I looked at my Instagram. I said, oh man, that’s the death of the SEC Championship in Atlanta. SEC would no longer have a SEC Championship. Oh my goodness, the nostalgia of that in that December weekend. Oh my goodness. “But then I started to realize, I said, hold on. Let me dive a little deeper. I love it. Because the reality of it all is this. There would never be another undefeated college football team ever. Think about it. Throughout this format, teams get penalized for playing soft schedules. I like that. That’s all I wanted to see, I didn’t always have SEC bias, I didn’t necessarily care if it was big table, what I do care about is how did you get there? Now teams will be penalized for having a weakness in their schedule.” Newton was part of the SEC across his stints with the Florida Gators and Auburn. He knows how massive the conference championship games are, especially in the SEC. Newton himself had an iconic game in the Conference Championship game, where he scored 6 touchdowns to help Auburn advance to the National Championship game. The new format seems to not only help boost revenue for College Football, but also allow programs that have just missed out on the playoffs to make a push. In times where NIL is dominating the sport, the extra few spots for teams gives them a shot.
